summary.headline: Anand Rathi Wealth Q1 FY27 underlying PAT rose 24% YoY to INR116 crore, with AUM up 21% to INR1,06,300 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported its 19th consecutive quarter of profit growth, with underlying consolidated revenue (excluding fair value gains, ESOP and related tax) up 18% YoY to INR336 crore and PAT up 24% to INR116 crore, a 34.4% margin. Reported revenue and PAT including fair value gains were INR430 crore and INR163 crore, with INR96 crore of the other income being mark-to-market gain on the Anand Rathi Global Finance (ARGFL) holding. Net flows were INR2,743 crore in the quarter, and client attrition was 0.09% of AUM with zero RM attrition. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,415 crore revenue and INR460 crore PAT, with Q1 delivering 24% and 25% of these respectively. The call also covered a Board approval to apply for an AMC licence, a UK subsidiary, and a GIFT City licence in progress.

segments.name: Flagship wealth management (ARWL)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,06,300 crore, 13,941 client families after net addition of 1,600+ in last 12 months; client AUM attrition 0.09% in Q1 and zero RM attrition. AUM per RM described as rising, with 33 clients per RM.

segments.name: Digital wealth (B2B2C subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR2,526 crore, up 23% YoY; clients up 16% to 7,320.

segments.name: OFA (SaaS platform subsidiary)
segments.commentary: 6,890 subscribers and platform assets of INR1.66 lakh crore as of 30 June 2026.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Net equity MF sales of INR1,900 crore in Q1. Management cites FY26 market share of net flows at 2.3% (presented as 2.47%), up from 0.18% in FY19-20; distributor yield about 1.09% post-GST, with 1-3 bps possible pressure from TER changes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,415 crore and PAT guidance of INR460 crore reiterated; Q1 achieved 24% and 25% respectively.
Management modelled AUM growth of 20-25% p.a. over next 3 years: 10-12% from mark-to-market plus net sales of INR1,100-1,200 crore per month (about 1% of AUM per month).
Long-term target of about 4% share of AMFI Category II assets (around INR6 lakh crore in ~8-10 years), requiring 22-23% asset growth.
Board approved applying for an AMC licence; GIFT City licence in process (second stage underway).
capex_capacity: Board approved AMC licence application; first stage of licensing done, second stage in process per management.
UK subsidiary operations started in Q1; management said it would be built brick-by-brick, not scaled quickly.
Management cites capacity for about 6,500 new client families with existing RMs (33 clients per RM against capacity of ~50), plus 490 trained RMs and 100 more RMs about 60% ready.
Fund of funds in UK with 11 schemes listed there for UK participants.
demand_pricing: Net flows of INR2,743 crore in Q1 despite volatile markets; equity MF net sales INR1,900 crore.

Platinum families (INR50 crore+ bucket) about 230 vs 211 earlier; target 450-500 in two years. Upgrade rate from sub-INR5 crore to INR50 crore cohort guided at roughly 10-20% per quarter (management estimate).
Model portfolio of 14 mutual fund schemes beat Nifty by about 6% in Q1 (Nifty about 7%, portfolio about 7% after costs per management; figures as stated).

Structured products: management says ARGFL products dominate the mix; third-party share kept low for credit risk. Q1 MLD primary issuance INR2,187 crore (INR1,875 crore to group companies, INR312 crore third party), up from INR1,704 crore; secondary INR968 crore vs INR755 crore.
Client retention on three RM departures to a competitor: about 90% of INR758 crore assets retained as of June end (INR658.5 crore), excluding market movement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 update on Platinum families and how fast will the INR5-50 crore bucket upgrade?
qa_highlights.answer: Platinum families are about 230 vs 211 earlier, from 40-45 at launch about 2.5 years ago; upgrade rate estimated at 10-20% a quarter; management expects four-digit client counts in a few years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cap on AUM per RM?
qa_highlights.answer: No cap; management says AUM per RM should keep rising while client attrition stays low (0.09%), and some RMs have reached INR500-1,500 crore. The figure was INR100 crore at listing.

qa_highlights.question: How is asset allocation managed in volatile markets and why not recommend gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the highest portfolio beta is 0.6-0.65 and it sells products it buys; it does not recommend gold given household gold holdings of about 28% of savings. Overall mix is about INR55,000 crore equity and INR4,500 crore debt plus structured products.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the other income of INR110 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR96 crore is mark-to-market gain on ARGFL holding, revalued semi-annually by a third-party investment banker; the rest is interest on surplus cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is there yield pressure from TER changes in mutual funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through is limited to 1-3 bps of its roughly 1.09% post-GST yield, and scale gives bargaining power; it has no plans to recommend stocks, PMS or long-only AIFs currently.

qa_highlights.question: Will ARWL enter investment banking or other capital market businesses?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will pursue only an AMC licence and no investment banking, focusing on intergenerational wealth rather than transaction-driven capital management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term AUM growth plan and how is it sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% AUM growth from embedded client returns, capacity in existing RMs, new RMs and penetration, citing 90-95% confidence; the 4% Category II target implies 22-23% growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the RBI bank guarantee circular on derivatives volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views the circular as positive, expecting reduced high-frequency trading volumes, and sees negligible or positive impact on ARWL.
